title: Restriction does not increase decision-tree depth
statement:
Let $T$ be a decision tree on $n$ Boolean variables, and let $\rho$ be a restriction on those variables, that is, an assignment giving each variable either a fixed Boolean value or leaving it free. Let $T|_\rho$ denote the tree obtained by collapsing every branch whose query variable is fixed by $\rho$ into the corresponding subtree while keeping the unrestricted branches intact, and write $\mathrm{depth}$ for the maximum length of a path from the root to a leaf. Then
\[
\mathrm{depth}(T|_\rho) \le \mathrm{depth}(T).
\]
hypotheses_covered: T is a decision tree on n Boolean variables
rho is a restriction on those n variables
replaced:
For every decision tree $T$ and restriction $\rho$, the depth of the restricted tree
satisfies $\mathrm{depth}(\mathrm{dtRestrict}\,T\,\rho) \le \mathrm{depth}(T)$.
